You can already point `ngcc` at your `dist/libraries` folder if you wish... You just supply the `-s` option to `ngcc`. E.g.

```
ngcc -s dist/libraries --create-ivy-entry-points
```

That being said I believe that the work that @alan-agius4 has been doing to add async pre-processing of libraries by ngcc in CLI might already help this.

So thanks @petebacondarwin .
I have tried (right now) the `ngcc` with `-s` option and it works as aspected but:

after `ngcc` command we have library not ready to publish (after `ngcc` command we have library 'ivy' enabled).

So how to accomplish that flow on CI?

1. Build all for tests (without prod so ivy is enabled)
2. Test all libraries in a concurrencies way
3. Rebuild all with --prod flag
...
I guess it is going to be slower than now.

Another way could be:
1. Change `tsconfig` to link all libraries to projects folder
2. Test all libraries
3. Change back `tsconfig` to point libraries on dist folder
4. Build all with --prod flag

Any advice here?
Thanks.

I remember seeing advice (possibly from @alan-agius4) that one could make a copy of the dist folder as a post-build step before running ngcc on it. Then do your library release from the copied folder.

Hi @meriturva, 

**Issue 1: Parallel builds**
For this issue, what @petebacondarwin suggested in here https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/36119#issuecomment-600490685 is a correct approach. Currently, NGCC async in the CLI only processes `node_modules`.  @petebacondarwin, maybe we can add the feature to provide a stringified path mappings as argument in NGCC?

**Issue 2: Bulding, Testing and Publishing a VE libraries**
I think the best approach would be to;
- Building your library in VE
- Run `npm pack`
- Run ng test, which under the hood will call NGCC that will convert your library to Ivy
- `npm publish` using the tarball generated by `npm pack`

More info about `npm pack` and `npm publish` can be found here: https://docs.npmjs.com/cli-commands/pack.html and https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/publish

Actually before point 3: `run ng test (concurrency way)` we have to call ngcc for all libraries we have with `-s` param.

am I right?
Given the rest of the discussion here - yes. But only if you want to run your tests in parallel.
I want to emphases what @petebacondarwin said, that this will only be needed if you run tests in parallel and not when running them concurrently.

Thanks for your help and ideas!
I will test new flow and give you a feedback if necessary.

I have to reopen the issue.
We have now all the libraries prepared with `ngcc` command as described above.

But when we run `ng test` file `__ngcc_lock_file__` still created and so no way to run tests in parallel.

How to avoid the creation of lock file during test phase?
